scope: Frozen assigned titles and complete ItemBodies, matching local source and HTML, receipt metadata, and every receipt-listed screenshot tile. No live routes.

review_method.rendering: All 333 receipt-listed PNG tiles were individually opened with tools.view_image at original resolution; no collage or downscaled substitute was used. Each tile below is attested individually and has a matching observed SHA-256.
review_method.source_snapshot_html: All 174 frozen titles and complete ItemBodies were reviewed in the captured local HTML tile sequences; source lines for diagram candidates were checked against frozen snapshots. Every frozen snapshot hash equals its assigned source hash; every local HTML hash equals its assignment hash.
review_method.boundary: Local-only and read-only audit. No item, application, or publication-status changes.

findings.rationale: The example claims a concrete convex pentagon, validates its boundary, and explicitly uses the two diagonals from v0 to form three triangles before comparing the resulting area with the shoelace sum. A labeled polygon would let readers check the cyclic order, triangulation, orientation, and area decomposition at a glance.

concrete_maps_and_relations.vertices: v0=(0,0), v1=(4,0), v2=(5,2), v3=(2,4), v4=(0,3), cyclic counterclockwise

findings.diagram_spec: Draw the five vertices in order, label each coordinate and directed boundary edge, draw diagonals v0-v2 and v0-v3 as interior edges, and label the three triangle areas 4, 8, 3; optionally place shoelace total 30/2 alongside.
findings.certainty: candidate for owner review; no production/source edit made

findings.rationale: This landmark example rotates the explicit sine arch around the x-axis and reports its surface area. A profile plus revolution sketch would show the radius function, axis, endpoint collapse, and angular parameter that the formula integrates.

concrete_maps_and_relations.profile: r(x)=sin x, 0≤x≤π; r>0 for 0<x<π and r(0)=r(π)=0

findings.diagram_spec: Show y=sin x from x=0 to π in profile, rotate around labeled x-axis, and include the generated horn-like surface with endpoint circles collapsed to the axis; label radial distance sin x and angular θ.
findings.certainty: candidate for owner review; no production/source edit made

findings.rationale: The example’s point is that a cylinder boundary is covered by two differently parameterized polar caps and four quarter-cylinder patches, with seams arranged to satisfy compatibility and coordinate-adapted coverage. A labeled patch diagram makes the six-piece decomposition and seams inspectable.

concrete_maps_and_relations.side_patches: σj(θ,z)=(R cosθ,R sinθ,z), θ∈Jj, 0≤z≤H; Jj=[jπ/2,(j+1)π/2], j=0,1,2,3

findings.diagram_spec: Draw the cylinder with top/bottom caps and four side sectors separated at θ=0,π/2,π,3π/2,2π; mark cap parameter rays (different positive-axis seam directions on top and bottom), all quarter sectors, and z=0,H. Add a legend of each map.
findings.certainty: candidate for owner review; no production/source edit made

findings.rationale: The false claim is about global injectivity of the spherical-coordinate map; its failures are the angular seam, collapse of azimuth at both poles, and collapse of all angles at r=0. One domain-to-image diagram would explain these distinct fibers and connect them to the vanishing Jacobian.

concrete_maps_and_relations.map: S(r,φ,θ)=(r sinφ cosθ, r sinφ sinθ, r cosφ)
concrete_maps_and_relations.jacobian: det DS = r² sinφ; zero at r=0 and φ∈{0,π}

findings.diagram_spec: Pair a spherical-coordinate box with identified θ=0/2π faces to a sphere; mark the polar edges and r=0 face collapsing to axis/poles/origin, and annotate Jacobian zero loci.
